raw_response:
I have farmed here in Quzhou for 50 years, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked for me last year and what I saw on nearby fields, then I adjust a little for cost and water. My land is 11.6 mu, not small but not big either, so I cannot gamble. Cotton is still my main crop, so I will keep the biggest share there. With well irrigation in hand, I will feed cotton and wheat a bit heavier because if those two lose yield, the loss hurts more than spending a few more yuan on fertilizer. For maize I will keep a solid rate because it responds fast if water and fertilizer are there. Millet and mungbean cost less, so I will use less fertilizer there, especially nitrogen on mungbean, because that crop can carry itself better and I mainly want steady output, not fancy management. I will plough the wheat and cotton ground, because I want the base fertilizer turned in well, and I will use rotary tillage on the smaller summer crops to save labor and time. I will not cut fertilizer too hard this year; when I am unsure, I would rather be a little heavy than watch the field go pale and lose harvest.
